units.title: The Passive Voice
units.intro: We use the passive (be + past participle) when the action is more important than the person who does it.
items: Dates are grown in Saudi Arabia.
Oranges are grown in warm countries.
The bridge was built last year.
These stories were written by a famous writer.
The letters were written in Arabic.

acts.title: Active or passive?
rows: The milk was drunk by the cat.

units.title: used to
units.intro: We use used to + verb for habits in the past that are not true now.
items: When I was little, I used to play with a teddy bear.
He used to drink milk every night.
My grandparents used to live in a small village.
We used to live in Jeddah.
I didn't use to like vegetables, but now I do.

acts.title: Choose the right word
rows: When I was five, I ... to sleep early.

acts.title: Then and now
rows: Grandpa used to write letters. Now he ...
People used to travel by camel. Now they travel by ...
I used to be short. Now I am ...
My brother used to cry a lot. Now he ...

units.title: as … as
units.intro: We use as + adjective + as when two things are the same, and not as … as when they are different.
items: Ali is as tall as Omar.
My bike is not as fast as a car.
A cat is not as heavy as an elephant.

acts.title: as or than?
rows: Sara is as old ... Mona. Both are twelve.
A mouse is not as big ... a cat.
My bag is as heavy ... yours.

acts.title: What does it mean?
rows: Omar is as tall as Ali.
A bike is not as fast as a plane.
Tea is as hot as coffee.
My room is not as big as yours.

units.title: have to / don't have to
units.intro: have to means it is necessary. don't have to means it is not necessary.
items: We have to wear a uniform at school.
I have to do my homework.
A doctor has to work at night sometimes.
She has to wake up early.
It is Friday. We don't have to go to school.
You don't have to pay. It's free.

acts.title: Choose the right words
rows: The museum is free. You ... pay.
Drivers ... stop at a red light.
It's a holiday. We ... get up early.
You ... wash your hands before eating.

units.title: Question Tags
units.intro: A question tag is a short question at the end of a sentence. After a positive sentence we use a negative tag, and after a negative sentence we use a positive tag.
items: It's a sunny day, isn't it?

units.title: Phrasal Verbs
units.intro: A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word (up, off, for …). Together they have a new meaning.
items: I am looking for my glasses.
Please turn off the lights when you leave.
My sister takes care of our baby brother.
We take care of our plants.

acts.title: Choose the phrasal verb
rows: Please ... the lights. We are saving energy.
I can't find my pen. I'm ... it.

units.title: Reading Time
units.intro: Read the stories, then answer the questions.

acts.title: The Old Mosque
acts.html:
The Old Mosque 🕌

This mosque was built more than one hundred years ago.
It was made of stone and wood.
People used to pray there every day.
Last year, it was repaired by the people of the town.
Now it is as beautiful as it was in the past.

acts.title: Answer
rows: more than one hundred years ago

acts.title: A Busy Morning
acts.html:
A Busy Morning ⏰

Every morning, Khalid has to wake up at six.
He turns off his alarm and prays Fajr.
Then he takes care of his little brother and gives him breakfast.
Khalid doesn't have to walk to school, because his father drives him.
He is a helpful boy, isn't he?

acts.title: Answer
rows: What time does Khalid have to wake up?
What does he do after he turns off his alarm?
Who does he take care of?
Why doesn't he have to walk to school?
